title: Capacity: Litres
seo_title: Capacity – Primary 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Measure capacity in litres; compare the capacity of containers; read scales on measuring jugs. (summary of the NERDC Primary 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 maths worksheets on capacity: litres and millilitres, reading measuring jugs, comparing containers and capacity problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Capacity is how much a container can hold.
  • We measure it in litres (l). Small amounts are in millilitres (ml): 1 litre = 1,000 ml.
  • Read the scale at the top of the water level.

Examples

Example

A bucket holds 10 litres. How much do 3 buckets hold?

10 × 3

Answer: 30 litres

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the wrong markFind what each mark stands for.
Mixing litres and millilitresUse the same unit.
Thinking a tall container always holds moreA wide container can hold more.

items.q: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth. So 1 l = 1,000 ml.

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a teaspoon holds?
items.e: A teaspoon holds only a little, about 5 millilitres. 5 l would fill a big bucket halfway.

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a mug holds?
items.e: A mug of tea is about 300 millilitres. 300 l would fill a bath.

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a bucket holds?
items.e: A bucket holds about 10 litres. 10 ml is only two teaspoons.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a slice of bread?
items.e: A slice of bread is light, so grams are the best unit. Kilograms are for heavy things, and centimetres measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much water a bathtub holds?
items.e: How much water a bathtub holds is a liquid volume. Liquid volume is measured in litres. Grams and kilograms measure mass, and metres measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a bag of potatoes?
items.e: A bag of potatoes is heavy, so kilograms are the best unit. Liters measure liquid, and metres measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a pencil?
items.e: A pencil is light. You could hold many in one hand, so grams are the best unit. Kilograms are for heavy things, and centimetres measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a strawberry?
items.e: A strawberry is very light, about as heavy as a few paper clips. Light things are measured in grams. Kilograms are for heavy things, and centimetres measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a key?
items.e: A key is small and light, so measure it in grams. Kilograms are for heavy things, and centimetres measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a dog?
items.e: A dog is heavy, so measure its mass in kilograms. Liters measure liquid, and metres measure length.

items.e: The water in a fish tank is a liquid volume, so use litres. Grams and kilograms measure mass, and metres measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a bicycle?
items.e: A bicycle is heavy. Heavy things are measured in kilograms. Liters measure liquid, and metres measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much water a kitchen sink holds?
items.e: The water in a sink is a liquid volume, so use litres. Grams and kilograms measure mass, and metres measure length.

items.q: A rain barrel had 39 L of water. A storm added 23 L. How much water is in the barrel now?
items.e: Add the water that came in: 39 + 23 = 62 L.

items.q: Aminat puts a book with a mass of 334 g and a pencil case with a mass of 138 g in her backpack. What is the total mass of the two things?
items.e: Put the masses together: 334 + 138 = 472 g.

items.q: A bag of dog food has 20 kg of food. Sani's dog eats 4 kg each week. How many weeks will the bag last?
items.e: How many groups of 4 kg are in 20 kg? 20 ÷ 4 = 5 weeks.

items.q: A bag had 940 g of flour. Amaka used 264 g to bake bread. How much flour is left in the bag?
items.e: Flour was used up, so subtract: 940 − 264 = 676 g.

items.q: A box holds 7 toy cars that all have the same mass. Together the cars have a mass of 210 g. What is the mass of 1 toy car?
items.e: Share the mass equally: 210 ÷ 7 = 30 g.

items.q: A coach mixes 15 L of sports drink. The coach pours the same amount into 3 coolers. How many litres go into each cooler?
items.e: Share equally: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 L in each cooler.

items.q: A bathtub had 134 L of water. Then 47 L drained out. How much water is left in the bathtub?
items.e: Water went out, so subtract: 134 − 47 = 87 L.

items.q: Ruth's bicycle has a mass of 16 kg. Her scooter has a mass of 4 kg. How much heavier is the bicycle?
items.e: “How much heavier” compares two masses, so subtract: 16 − 4 = 12 kg.

items.q: A puppy had a mass of 8 kg in the spring. Now it has a mass of 13 kg. How many kilograms did it gain?
items.e: Find the difference: 13 − 8 = 5 kg.

items.q: A baker uses 8 kg of flour each day. How many kilograms of flour does the baker use in 6 days?
items.e: 6 days of 8 kg: 6 × 8 = 48 kg.

items.q: A small wading pool holds 400 L when it is full. It has 304 L of water in it now. How many more litres are needed to fill it?
items.e: Find the missing part: 400 − 304 = 96 L.

items.q: A bucket holds 5 L. How many full buckets of water are needed to fill a tank that holds 40 L?
items.e: How many 5 L buckets make 40 L? 40 ÷ 5 = 8 buckets.

items.q: Abdullahi buys 6 bottles of water for a picnic. Each bottle holds 2 L. How many litres of water does he buy?
items.e: 6 bottles of 2 L: 6 × 2 = 12 L.

items.q: Kemi's backpack full of books has a mass of 6 kg. The empty backpack has a mass of 2 kg. What is the mass of the books?
items.e: Take away the backpack: 6 − 2 = 4 kg.

items.q: One egg has a mass of about 50 g. What is the mass of 6 eggs?
items.e: 6 equal groups of 50 g: 6 × 50 = 300 g.

items.q: Chinedu has 24 kg of potatoes. He puts them into 6 sacks with the same mass. What is the mass of each sack?
items.e: Share 24 kg equally into 6 sacks: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 kg.

items.q: A fish tank has 33 L of water. Tobi adds 18 L more. How much water is in the tank now?
items.e: Adding more means add: 33 + 18 = 51 L.

items.q: Victor picks 64 kg of apples. He packs them into 8 bags with the same mass. What is the mass of each bag?
items.e: Share equally: 64 ÷ 8 = 8 kg in each bag.

items.q: Hauwa's watering can holds 9 L. She fills it 3 times to water the garden. How many litres of water does she use?
items.e: 3 times 9 L: 3 × 9 = 27 L.

items.q: A store has 6 bags of rice. Each bag has a mass of 3 kg. What is the total mass of the rice?
items.e: 6 equal bags of 3 kg: 6 × 3 = 18 kg.
